When a country treats a restroom like a product launch, you notice.

I just read about Norway’s “world’s best toilets” program—tiny cabins that combine sleek design, eco‑friendly waste handling, and real‑time occupancy data. The government turned a basic amenity into a high‑touch experience, boosting traveler satisfaction and even cutting maintenance costs through predictive analytics.

It’s a reminder that the most overlooked UI—whether a button or a bathroom stall—can make or break user loyalty. In software we obsess over dashboards, but the same attention to frictionless, well‑maintained micro‑interactions can drive adoption at scale.

What low‑visibility feature in your stack could use a world‑class upgrade?
